questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Asymptotes of a Hyperbola Given Its Equation in Non-Standard Form
questions.problem: Find the asymptotes of the hyperbola ${y}^{2}-9{x}^{2}=9.$
questions.worked_solution:
The standard equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at the origin is

$$
\frac{{y}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

For a vertical hyperbola centered at the origin, the equations of the asymptotes are

$$
y=\pm \frac{a}{b}x.
$$

To rewrite the given equation in standard form, we divide both sides of the equation by $9$ and then simplify, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}-9{x}^{2} & =9 \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{9}-\frac{9{x}^{2}}{9} & =\frac{9}{9} \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{9}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{1} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have $a=\sqrt{9}=3$ and $b=\sqrt{1}=1.$

Therefore, the asymptotes of the hyperbola are

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\pm \frac{3}{1}x \\  & =\pm 3x.\end{aligned}
$$

The standard equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at the origin is

$$
\frac{{y}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

For a vertical hyperbola centered at the origin, the equations of the asymptotes are

$$
y=\pm \frac{a}{b}x.
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
a=\sqrt{64}=8,\,b=\sqrt{4}=2.
$$

Therefore, the asymptotes of the hyperbola are

$$

questions.problem: Find the asymptotes of the hyperbola $8{y}^{2}-25{x}^{2}=200.$
questions.worked_solution:
The standard equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at the origin is

$$
\frac{{y}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

For a vertical hyperbola centered at the origin, the equations of the asymptotes are

$$
y=\pm \frac{a}{b}x.
$$

To rewrite the given equation in standard form, we divide both sides of the equation by $200$ and then simplify, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}8{y}^{2}-25{x}^{2} & =200 \\ \frac{8{y}^{2}}{200}-\frac{25{x}^{2}}{200} & =\frac{200}{200} \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{25}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{8} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have $a=\sqrt{25}=5,$ and $b=\sqrt{8}=2\sqrt{2}.$

Therefore, the asymptotes of the hyperbola are $y=\pm \frac{5}{2\sqrt{2}}x=\pm \frac{5\sqrt{2}}{4}x.$
